analysis.title: GS Soria - Higher Rates = Bid for Quality
key_insights: The index is near all-time highs, but the market is rewarding quality underneath. The desk frames this as a shift in focus from growth to the composition of growth, not only a reaction to higher rates.

The desk expects the rate of change of growth to decelerate over the next 12 months in both AI and non-AI pockets of the economy. It sees this as a net positive backdrop for quality, since the factor tends to outperform as earnings growth rolls over.

The sector, industry and factor neutral Quality Pair Index (GSP1QUAL) is up 20% over the last 3 months to a 12m high on about 13% realized vol. The move was driven by a sharp selloff in the short leg (GSX1BFQS).

Quality is strongly negatively correlated to AI, momentum and beta exposure, so it can serve as a hedge to those crowded themes. Momentum positioning is at the 78th percentile on 5y and Beta at the 81st.

The desk continues to favor quality (GSP1QUAL) and defensives over cyclicals (short GSPUCYDE). It also likes shorting long duration pockets such as Low Quality Equities (GSXULOWQ), which it says is a cleaner rates expression than higher-beta alternatives (GSX1NPTC).
The quality bias is also emerging within AI. Mag-7 net positioning is at the highs and these megacaps are holding while lower-quality AI has been repriced.
Hyperscalers (GSXUHYPR) have materially outperformed their own credit (GSUCHS30), with equities moving higher as spreads widened.
Long GSP1QUAL vs short the Momentum Pair (GSP1MOMO) is up 55% in 2026, following a 60% rout.
Technicals in the Quality Factor are stretched: RSI of 83 after the factor was up in 16 of the last 18 trading sessions.
A softer CPI print or evidence that rates are peaking could trigger a reversal and a relief rally in longer duration, lower-quality names.
